rv.q: As gleefully as the musical follows the formula of the rom-com genre, it also has a welcome comfort with ambiguity and, stashed up its sleeve, some psychological bombs. The action floats along so comfortably, both in and out of song, that it seems odd to interrupt that momentum with an intermission....
I am loath to overpraise this little gem. I know sophisticates will find it thin, predictable, and often unconvincing in its details.

Tutty’s appealing looks, pure voice, comic instincts, and obvious acting skills, and somehow resemblance to a living Teletubby make him the huge plus for a vital Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York) run.
This is a show so charming, so adorable, that you can easily overlook its flaws.
A new rom-com musical begins promisingly but loses its way somewhere between JFK Airport and midtown Manhattan.
What ultimately makes Two Strangers such a winning Broadway arrival is its belief that tenderness is still theatrical currency.
This is a charming little show (which definitely doesn't need to be two hours and twenty minutes long)
Like a Hallmark movie, “Two Strangers” boasts enough humor and whimsy to be sweet and superficially appealing, but at the end, all we’re left with is the superficial.

cn.t: Critics largely embrace this modest British rom-com musical for its tenderness and charm, though some find it overlong. The two leads earn widespread praise for their chemistry in this old-fashioned crowd-pleaser.
